key_insight: UniMedSeg unifies visual examples, geometric prompts, language instructions, and 2D/3D medical images in one Transformer-based framework for multi-paradigm segmentation.
clinical_relevance: A single model that handles multiple segmentation workflows could simplify deployment and improve consistency across diverse medical imaging tasks.
method: Maps heterogeneous prompts and images into a shared sequence space
Uses Decoupled Split Attention to reduce long-sequence attention cost to linear complexity
Trains on a large corpus from 27 public datasets without task-specific fine-tuning
evidence_signal: The paper reports state-of-the-art performance across visual in-context, interactive, and language-guided segmentation on held-out tasks after extensive training and evaluation on 27 public datasets.
watch_item: Real-world adoption may depend on whether the unified model remains robust across scanners, institutions, and rare anatomical edge cases beyond the benchmark datasets.
paper_title: UniMedSeg: Unified In-Context Learning for Multi-Paradigm 2D/3D Medical Image Segmentation
